steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Geological hazards arise from Earth processes that pose risk to people and property: landslides, subsidence, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, flooding | Key Fact: Landslides (mass movement): rockfalls, slides, flows and creep; triggered by heavy rain, earthquakes, undercutting, or human activity | Key Fact: Factors affecting slope stability: angle, geology (weak layers, joints), water content (lubricates and adds weight), vegetation (stabilises or destabilises) | Key Fact: Subsidence: ground sinking due to dissolution of limestone (sinkholes), mining, or groundwater extraction

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from geological hazard processes, and one past-paper question.
